TITLE: REGULATIONS GOVERNING STUDENT ATTENDANCE AND LEAVE OF ABSENCE

1. MINIMUM ATTENDANCE REQUIREMENT
1.1 Every registered student is expected to attend 100% of the lectures, tutorials, and practical laboratory sessions scheduled for each registered course.
1.2 To be eligible to appear for the End-Semester Examination in any course, a student must secure a minimum attendance of 75% in aggregate across all lectures, tutorials, and laboratories of that specific course.

cure a minimum attendance of 75% in aggregate across all lectures, tutorials, and laboratories of that specific course.
1.3 Students with attendance below 75% in any course will receive an Attendance Shortage Notice and shall be officially debarred from appearing in the End-Semester Examination for that particular course.
1.4 Debarred students will receive a grade of 'SA' (Shortage of Attendance), which carries 0 grade points, and must re-register for the course in a subsequent semester or summer term.

CAMPUS UNIVERSITY DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING
COURSE CODE: CS201
COURSE TITLE: DATA STRUCTURES AND ALGORITHMS
CATEGORY: University Syllabus and Course Details
ACADEMIC YEAR: 2025-2026

1. LINEAR DATA STRUCTURES
1.1 Arrays and Linked Lists:
- Singly, Doubly, and Circular Linked Lists. Insertion, deletion, reversal, and cycle detection (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare algorithm).
1.2 Stacks and Queues:
- Stack operations (LIFO) for function call stacks, parenthesis matching, infix to postfix conversion.
- Queue operations (FIFO), Circular Queue, Double-Ended Queue (Deque), and Priority Queue using Binary Heaps.

version.
- Queue operations (FIFO), Circular Queue, Double-Ended Queue (Deque), and Priority Queue using Binary Heaps.

2. TREES AND SEARCHING
2.1 Binary Search Tree (BST):
- Binary tree where left subtree keys < node key < right subtree keys. In-order traversal produces sorted keys.
- Search, Insertion, Deletion time complexity: O(h), where h is height. In balanced BST, h = O(log n).
2.2 Self-Balancing Trees (AVL Trees and Red-Black Trees):
- AVL trees maintain balance factor = height(left) - height(right) in {-1, 0, 1} through Single (LL, RR) and Double (LR, RL) rotations. Guarantees O(log n) worst-case time for search, insert, and delete.

ugh Single (LL, RR) and Double (LR, RL) rotations. Guarantees O(log n) worst-case time for search, insert, and delete.

3. GRAPH ALGORITHMS
3.1 Graph Representations:
- Adjacency Matrix: O(V^2) space, O(1) edge lookup.
- Adjacency List: O(V + E) space, efficient for sparse graphs.
3.2 Graph Traversals:
- Breadth-First Search (BFS): Uses queue, finds shortest path in unweighted graphs, O(V + E) time.
- Depth-First Search (DFS): Uses recursion/stack, topological sort, cycle detection in directed graphs, O(V + E) time.
3.3 Shortest Path Algorithms:
- Dijkstra's Algorithm: Greedy single-source shortest path for non-negative edge weights using Min-Heap, O((V + E) log V) time.
- Bellman-Ford Algorithm: Handles negative edge weights, detects negative cycles, O(V * E) time.

((V + E) log V) time.
- Bellman-Ford Algorithm: Handles negative edge weights, detects negative cycles, O(V * E) time.

4. ALGORITHM DESIGN TECHNIQUES
4.1 Dynamic Programming (DP):
- Characterized by Overlapping Subproblems and Optimal Substructure. Top-down with Memoization or Bottom-up with Tabulation (e.g., 0/1 Knapsack, Longest Common Subsequence).
4.2 Greedy Algorithms:
- Makes locally optimal choice at each stage (e.g., Fractional Knapsack, Huffman Coding, Kruskal's/Prim's Minimum Spanning Tree).

CAMPUS UNIVERSITY DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING
COURSE CODE: CS301
COURSE TITLE: OPERATING SYSTEMS PRINCIPLES
CATEGORY: University Syllabus and Course Details
ACADEMIC YEAR: 2025-2026

1. PROCESS MANAGEMENT AND CPU SCHEDULING
1.1 Process vs Thread:
- Process: Program in execution with its own address space, PCB (Process Control Block), text, data, heap, and stack.
- Thread: Lightweight unit of CPU utilization sharing code, data, and OS resources with peer threads, but having its own stack and registers.
1.2 CPU Scheduling Algorithms:
- First-Come First-Served (FCFS): Non-preemptive, suffers from Convoy Effect.
- Shortest Job First (SJF): Optimal average waiting time, but suffers from starvation of long jobs.

from Convoy Effect.
- Shortest Job First (SJF): Optimal average waiting time, but suffers from starvation of long jobs.
- Round Robin (RR): Preemptive using time quantum, fair sharing, optimal for interactive systems.
- Multi-Level Feedback Queue (MLFQ): Dynamically adjusts process priorities based on burst behavior.

2. SYNCHRONIZATION AND DEADLOCKS
2.1 Critical Section Problem:
- Requirements: Mutual Exclusion, Progress, Bounded Waiting.
- Synchronization primitives: Mutex Locks, Semaphores (Counting and Binary), Monitored Condition Variables.
2.2 Deadlock Coffman Conditions:
- Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.
- Avoidance: Banker's Algorithm ensures system never enters an unsafe state.

d and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.
- Avoidance: Banker's Algorithm ensures system never enters an unsafe state.

3. MEMORY MANAGEMENT
3.1 Paging and Virtual Memory:
- Logical address translated to physical address via Page Table using TLB (Translation Lookaside Buffer).
- Page Fault: Interrupt raised when referenced page is not in physical RAM, triggers demand paging swap from disk.
- Page Replacement Algorithms: FIFO, Optimal (Belady's), Least Recently Used (LRU), Clock algorithm.

CAMPUS UNIVERSITY DEPARTMENT OF COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING
COURSE CODE: CS303
COURSE TITLE: COMPUTER NETWORKS
CATEGORY: University Syllabus and Course Details
ACADEMIC YEAR: 2025-2026

1. APPLICATION LAYER PROTOCOLS
1.1 DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol):
- Definition: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) is a network management client-server protocol used to dynamically assign IP addresses, subnet masks, default gateways, and DNS server addresses to client devices joining a network.
- Purpose: Eliminates manual IP address configuration on every individual host, prevents IP address conflicts, and enables efficient reuse of IP addresses in local area networks (LANs).

ividual host, prevents IP address conflicts, and enables efficient reuse of IP addresses in local area networks (LANs).
- Port Numbers: DHCP operates over UDP. DHCP Server listens on UDP Port 67, and DHCP Client listens on UDP Port 68.
- The 4-Step DORA Process:
  (1) Discover (DHCPDISCOVER): Client broadcasts a message to locate available DHCP servers on the subnet.
  (2) Offer (DHCPOFFER): One or more DHCP servers unicast/broadcast an offer containing a reserved IP address and configuration parameters.
  (3) Request (DHCPREQUEST): Client broadcasts acceptance of the offered IP configuration and requests lease confirmation.
  (4) Acknowledge (DHCPACK): Server confirms the lease, commits the IP address binding in its database, and client configures its network interface.

Server confirms the lease, commits the IP address binding in its database, and client configures its network interface.
- DHCP Lease Time: The temporary duration for which an assigned IP address is valid before the client must send a DHCPREQUEST to renew.

1.2 DNS (Domain Name System):
- Hierarchical, distributed naming system that translates human-readable domain names (e.g., campusmind.edu) into machine-readable IP addresses.
- Operates on UDP Port 53 for standard queries and TCP Port 53 for zone transfers.

1.3 HTTP and HTTPS:
- Hypertext Transfer Protocol (Port 80) and HTTPS (Port 443 with TLS/SSL encryption) for web resource delivery.

HTTPS:
- Hypertext Transfer Protocol (Port 80) and HTTPS (Port 443 with TLS/SSL encryption) for web resource delivery.

2. TRANSPORT LAYER PRINCIPLES
2.1 Transmission Control Protocol (TCP):
- Connection-oriented, reliable, byte-stream protocol with 3-way handshake (SYN, SYN-ACK, ACK), flow control via sliding window, and congestion control (Slow Start, Congestion Avoidance, Fast Retransmit).
2.2 User Datagram Protocol (UDP):
- Connectionless, lightweight, unreliable datagram service with minimal header overhead (8 bytes), ideal for real-time VoIP, streaming, and DNS/DHCP.

unreliable datagram service with minimal header overhead (8 bytes), ideal for real-time VoIP, streaming, and DNS/DHCP.

3. NETWORK LAYER AND ROUTING
3.1 IPv4 vs IPv6 Addressing:
- IPv4 uses 32-bit addresses divided into network and host portions using CIDR subnet notation.
- IPv6 uses 128-bit hexadecimal addresses providing 3.4 x 10^38 unique addresses, stateless address autoconfiguration (SLAAC), and built-in IPsec.
3.2 Routing Protocols:
- Intra-domain: OSPF (Open Shortest Path First, Link-State algorithm using Dijkstra) and RIP (Routing Information Protocol, Distance Vector using Bellman-Ford).
- Inter-domain: BGP (Border Gateway Protocol, Path Vector).
